To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) scalar field space curvature can lead to mixing between the light and heavy modes, even when the heavy modes are far above the scale of inflation and (2) the resulting non-decoupling can be a significant effect, even when the kinetic energy of the heavy fields is negligible compared to the potential.
the dynamics of a light scalar field is modified by a non-decoupling of a heavy field in the case of a non-flat field space.

the non-decoupling between light and heavy fields can be understood as a consequence of field-space curvature, that this mixing is generically present in models with multiple fields, and that the non-trivial effects of field-space curvature can be understood in terms of a simple geometrical argument that we present in this thesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of multiple scalar fields, which is a common feature in many models in cosmology and string theory.
the effects of field-space curvature on the dynamics of scalar fields and the implications of these effects for inflation and low energy compactifications of string theories.
the dynamics of scalar field perturbative fluctuations around a background trajectory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the scalar field dynamics is more complicated than the naive effective description would suggest.
the field space geometry can have a profound impact on the dynamics of the scalar fields and their perturbations.
the field space curvature can be a source of interesting effects in the low-energy effective theory, and that these effects can have important consequences for the dynamics of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the non-decoupling effect can lead to a non-trivial contribution in the low energy theory.

, in a multi-field theory with a non-trivial potential and field space curvature, the low-energy effective theory for the fields that drive the dynamics is not the same as the one that one would obtain if the fields that are decoupled in the limit of vanishing kinetic energy were ignored.
we have found that the dynamics of scalar fields in the presence of field space curvature can have a profound impact on the evolution of the light fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dynamics of the heavy modes cannot be neglected in the low energy limit, and the effective theory must include the full set of fields, even if they do not have a mass scale much lighter than the Planck scale.
the low energy effective field theory for the light degrees of freedom is not necessarily the same as the theory that one obtains by integrating out the heavy modes.
field space curvature is not a mere artifact of a particular parametrization of the fields, but can lead to non-trivial physical effects.
